title: Marcos breaks ground on P2.2-B water supply project in Iloilo City
summary: President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. broke ground Friday on the P2.2-billion Jalaur Bulk Water Supply Project in Sta. Barbara, Iloilo, which is expected to deliver up to 86 million liters per…

blocks.text: President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. broke ground Friday on the P2.2-billion Jalaur Bulk Water Supply Project in Sta. Barbara, Iloilo, which is expected to deliver up to 86 million liters per day upon completion.
Speaking at the groundbreaking activity at the Metro Iloilo Bulk Water Facility in Barangay Talanghauan, Marcos said the project will increase water supply in the area by 2029.

"Water is essential to our health, to our livelihoods, the growth of our communities, and the food that we produce, to the businesses that we operate, so much of our daily, our very lives for that matter depend on having a sufficient and reliable water supply," Marcos said.

"Once completed, the project will provide an additional capacity of 86 million liters per day for Iloilo City and its seven districts, bringing the combined capacity to 136 million liters per day. With this additional supply, the Metro Iloilo Water District (MWID) aims to double its water service connections from 52,000 presently to 150,000 by 2029," the President added.

The P2.2-billion project, Marcos said, will complement the dams of Jalaur Multi-purpose Project Stage 2, which he inaugurated in July 2024. These systems are expected to improve water pressure and provide round-the-clock access to safe drinking water.

Marcos said MWID's coverage is just at 30% of households in Iloilo city, as drought associated with El Niño has exacerbated water shortages and placed further pressure on our existing water resources.

"As we now address the immediate challenges that are presented to us by El Niño, we must also look beyond that. As of the 5th of November, three major river irrigation systems in Iloilo have already reported significant declines in water levels. And that's why I've directed our concerned government agencies to use irrigation dams to supplement bulk water supply projects and to strengthen water security, especially in underserved areas," Marcos said.

Metro Pacific Water Chairman Manny Pangilinan, who also present during the groundbreaking, said the project will make the Metro Pacific-funded desalination plant in Iloilo city as a plug-and-play combo of power and water.

"For families, that means safer water at home. For businesses, it means room to grow. Any city that wants new offices and factories must be able to promise more reliable water first," Pangilinan said.

"On the surface, this appears to be a story only about pipes and permits. But when government and private sector have the will to engage in complex conversations about who does what—and actually choose to execute—things get done. This is what we need more of in our country," Pangilinan added.
Marcos agreed with Pangilinan, saying that water from the Jalaur River will travel through the high-line canal to a designated tapping point.

"From the tapping point here, it will be conveyed to a treatment facility. It will then be made safe for consumption before being distributed to our communities, to our households," Marcos said. — VDV, GMA News
